text:
incident-bot: @Mona on-call triggered: GPU pool 'inference-east-1-gpu-a' high queue depth and driver errors. Severity: P1. Paging SRE.

Mona (SRE): seeing it. queue growth +420% over 5m, token throttle spiking. Investigating.

Raj (Eng-Infra): getting alerts too. Autoscaler failed to add nodes: API error 403 quota.limit_exceeded in cloud. Logs show 'scale request rejected'.

Evan (Runtime): on the runtime side we have repeated CUDA/Xid 13 and several llm-worker OOMs. Kernel messages show "NVRM: Xid (13):..." and processes being killed.

Tilly (Support): multiple customers reporting timeouts for generation endpoints. Triage: customer A (fintech-prod) saw 503s, B (chatbot-saas) has degraded latency, random</> failures for C (analytics). Putting together impact list.

Mona (SRE): quick status: queue backlog ~6k reqs, tail latency >5s, token throttles engaged. Autoscaler attempted 6x, only 2 new nodes provisioned then cloud denied further requests.

Oncall Backup (SRE): pinged cloud infra to check quota increase. Also can we temporarily reroute lower-priority traffic to cpu fallback? 

Raj (Eng-Infra): I can flip routing for non-paid/low-priority route to cpu-hosted model. Doing that now - will take ~90s to propagate.

Evan (Runtime): digging into driver logs. Stack traces show recurring oom killer on userland process 'inferd' and repeated Xid 13 from gpu driver. Suspect a bad kernel module + runaway model batches.

Mona (SRE): mitigation plan attempt 1: 1) cordon nodes reporting frequent Xid; 2) drain and restart nvidia driver on those nodes; 3) scale down aggressive batch sizes for high-concurrency routes; 4) route some traffic to lower-quality fallback model.

Tilly (Support): I'll draft a short status for customers: "We're investigating increased errors and latency in inference-east-1; mitigation in progress. No data loss reported."

incident-bot: action items logged in incident issue: https://rwd/incident/1793051234

Evan (Runtime): commands I'm running (paste):
```
# show Xid events
sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200 | grep -i xid
# show oom kills
dmesg | grep -i "Out of memory"
# worker pids
ps aux | grep inferd
```

Mona (SRE): I see 3 nodes with repeated Xid 13 in last 10m: gpu-41, gpu-42, gpu-47. I'm cordoning gpu-41 and gpu-42 now.

Raj (Eng-Infra): cloud responded: temporary quota hold due to automated safety rule because of rapid scale. They can unblock but need manual approval — requested escalation.

Oncall Backup (SRE): while cloud approval pending, can we reduce target utilization threshold so autoscaler will add smaller instances? Might avoid hitting safety rule.

Raj (Eng-Infra): yes changing policy to allow smaller instance types and lower required min-cpu might succeed. Applying policy change.

Evan (Runtime): restarted nvidia-driver on gpu-41 and gpu-42; however gpu-47 is flapping on registration, kernel oops present. I'm isolating it from LB.

Mona (SRE): draining unhealthy nodes reduced active GPU capacity by ~25% but removed noisy failures; queue still high but stable growth slowed to +30%/5m.

Tilly (Support): updated customers: short note sent to affected accounts, flagged high-severity. CS synced with legal for any compliance notes.

incident-bot: PagerDuty escalation to Eng-Infra and Runtime tiers sent.

Mona (SRE): temporary triage measures done. Next mitigation: 1) reduce max-concurrency per-worker from 8->4, 2) set per-customer rate limits for free-tier, 3) enable model fallback for low-priority traffic. Executing.

Evan (Runtime): applied concurrency cap and lowered default batch size param. Early signs: per-worker memory usage down ~35%, fewer OOMs.

Raj (Eng-Infra): cloud approved quota bump for our account; adding 4x small GPU instances. Should start provisioning in ~3m.

Mona (SRE): good. Once new capacity ready, we'll rebalance traffic and de-cordon nodes one at a time after verification.

Oncall Backup (SRE): handoff note for next shift (copying): issues: driver Xid 13 + OOMs caused effective capacity loss; autoscaler hit cloud safety rule; mitigation: drained noisy nodes, restarted drivers, lowered concurrency/batches, requested quota bump, provisioning small instances, routing low-priority to cpu. Outstanding: monitor for node flaps, confirm new instances register cleanly, postmortem owners.

Tilly (Support): customer update: "Mitigations in progress. We have added capacity and reduced error rates for most customers. We'll follow up with RCA and timeline by EOD." Want approval on wording?

Mona (SRE): approved. Add note: if any regulated account needs more detail, route to security & compliance.

Evan (Runtime): after restart we still see one Xid on gpu-47 and kernel oops. I'll schedule a forced repro test on a mirror node later to capture driver stack trace. For now it's isolated.

Raj (Eng-Infra): new small instances are up and have registered. LB balancing starting to reduce queue by ~45%.

Mona (SRE): monitoring: queue now down from 6k -> 1.5k over 18m since initial paging, error rate down 82%. Keeping this thread for final wrap and handoff.

incident-bot: incident severity updated to "degraded". Please fill postmortem template: https://rwd/pm/incident-template

Oncall Backup (SRE): I will take follow-up ownership for the next 3 hours to watch for regressions. Handing off now to Oncall Backup (SRE).

Mona (SRE): thanks. Final note for handoff: collect driver versions on affected nodes, check kernel update cadence, consider autoscaler policy change to avoid safety-rule-triggered denies, postmortem owner: Evan (Runtime). Closing active paging.

Tilly (Support): I'll keep customers updated and move to post-incident comms. Marking support:monitoring.

incident-bot: thread closed for paging. Please update incident issue with timeline and tags.
